query: Consider the following context: The combination of elevated temperature and tribo-corrosion leads to the accelerated degradation of structural components used in many extreme environments. Recently developed high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with multiple principal elements have the potential for superior degradation resistance compared with presently used structural alloys. In that context, which material can be used for superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) will exhibit superior resistance to tribo-corrosion degradation than conventional structural alloys, such as duplex stainless steel, due to its dual-phase microstructure which promotes the formation of a protective oxide barrier under high-temperature and mechanically abrasive conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: A dual-phase microstructure consisting of FCC and BCC (or B2) phases in the as-prepared AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA.
generation.intervention: Subjecting the alloy to a combined environment of elevated temperature and corrosive molten salt conditions while applying mechanical wear (tribological stress).
generation.conditions: Temperatures ranging from 450 °C to 650 °C in a corrosive medium (e.g., molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl2 salt) with tribological loading simulating friction or sliding wear.
generation.structural_mediator: The dual-phase microstructure, where the protective FCC (or FCC-like) phase enriches noble elements and forms a passivating oxide layer that shields the more reactive BCC/B2 phase, thus reducing overall corrosion and wear.
generation.mechanism: Under combined high-temperature and mechanical wear conditions, the selective dissolution of the less noble phase is minimized by the formation of a robust protective oxide layer from the noble enriched phase. This dual action reduces both electrochemical degradation and mechanical material loss, thereby limiting tribo-corrosion.
generation.predicted_outcome: The EHEA will display a lower overall degradation (reduced material loss and wear rates) compared to conventional alloys like DS2205 under identical test conditions.
generation.baseline: Conventional alloys (e.g., duplex stainless steel 2205) that demonstrate higher corrosion rates and more pronounced tribo-corrosion degradation in similar high-temperature corrosive environments.
generation.boundary: The advantage may be limited by extreme conditions that exceed the alloy’s mechanical or chemical stability, such as excessively high corrosive activity or wear forces that may disrupt the protective oxide layer integrity.
generation.uncertainty: While corrosion data under molten salt conditions support enhanced performance, the precise effect size under combined tribological and corrosive stresses remains to be quantified. It is also uncertain how processing variations might influence the protective dual-phase behavior in actual service conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare test coupons of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA and a conventional duplex stainless steel (e.g., DS2205). Expose them simultaneously in a controlled test rig that simulates tribological wear (e.g., sliding or reciprocating motion against a counterface) under molten salt conditions at temperatures of 450 °C and 650 °C. Measure mass loss, wear track depth, and surface degradation over a predetermined time period.
measurements: Wear track depth and morphology (via SEM or optical profilometry)
Surface composition and oxide layer analysis (by EDS, XPS)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA does not demonstrate a statistically significant reduction in combined wear and corrosion rates compared to the duplex stainless steel under identical test conditions, the hypothesis of superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance is falsified.

cited_evidence.text:
Unlike other conventional alloys based on a “principal element,” high-entropy alloy (HEA) is a unique material that maintains a random solid solution structure without forming intermetallic compounds in operating temperatures due to its high configurational entropy [1] – [3] . It also has outstanding physical and chemical properties, which makes it a potential replacement for traditional metallic materials, and it has recently been referred to as a multi-principal element alloy (MPEA) or compositionally concentrated alloy (CCA) [4] – [9] .

As attention in HEAs increases, many studies have been conducted to explore its mechanical, physical and chemical properties [10] – [15] . In particular, equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA, which was the first developed HEA, is the most studied because of its excellent combination of tensile strength and elongation along with excellent fracture toughness and corrosion resistance [6] , [16] – [21] . However, despite the advantages of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA, many issues arise owing to its low yield strength and costly and complex thermomechanical processing (i.e., multiple casting → hot rolling → homogenization → cold rolling → annealing → cutting, etc.

Abstract Dual-phase high entropy alloys have recently attracted widespread attention as advanced structural materials due to their unique microstructure, excellent mechanical properties, and corrosion resistance. However, their molten salt corrosion behavior has not been reported, which is critical in evaluating their application merit in the areas of concentrating solar power and nuclear energy. Here, the molten salt corrosion behavior of AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) was evaluated in molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl 2 salt at 450 °C and 650 °C in comparison to conventional duplex stainless steel 2205 (DS2205). The EHEA showed a significantly lower corrosion rate of ~1 mm/year at 450 °C compared to ~8 mm/year for DS2205. Similarly, EHEA showed a lower corrosion rate of ~9 mm/year at 650 °C compared to ~20 mm/year for DS2205. There was selective dissolution of the body-centered cubic phase in both the alloys, B2 in AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 and α-Ferrite in DS2205. This was attributed to micro-galvanic coupling between the two phases in each alloy that was measured in terms of Volta potential difference using a scanning kelvin probe.
